Solution.S:
Let $y = \tan^{-1} \left( \sqrt{1 + x^2} - 1 \right)$. Differentiating:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{1 + (\sqrt{1 + x^2} - 1)^2} \cdot \frac{d}{dx} \left( \sqrt{1 + x^2} - 1 \right)$$
$$= \frac{1}{1 + (1 + x^2 + 1 - 2\sqrt{1 + x^2})} \cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{1 + x^2}} \cdot 2x$$
$$= \frac{1}{x^2 + 2 - 2\sqrt{1 + x^2}} \cdot \frac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}$$
$$= \frac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^2} \left( x^2 - 2\sqrt{1 + x^2} + 3 \right)}$$
Thus the correct option is B.
